title: Sudan (Darfur, 1591 regime) sanctions measures next come up for renewal — the one-month technical rollover resolution 2828 created after the Council split on expanding scope
source: NEWS: press.un.org/en/2026/sc16450.doc.htm ("Security Council Unanimously Adopts Resolution 2828 (2026), Renewing Sudan Sanctions for One Month"), fetched 2026-09-24 (via the model's browsing tool, not a direct HTTP fetch logged by this session — see Initial research method note) during this event's own initial research. The release states the Council "unanimously adopted resolution 2828 (2026)", extending the 1591 Sudan sanctions regime (targeted sanctions on Darfur plus an arms embargo) by one month and separately extending the Panel of Experts mandate to 9 November 2026. Corroborated by english.news.cn/20260912/7f4f2867b13148e7aa4f9899d218aac1/c.html (Xinhua, the source this id was originally proposed from), which quotes the measures date directly as "until Oct. 9, 2026", and by web-search-surfaced excerpts of securitycouncilreport.org's "What's in Blue" coverage of the same vote, which gives the same 9 October date for the measures. Estimate rather than confirmed on the same two grounds as the proposal: CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs carries no UN/diplomatic slot, and this session did not obtain the resolution's own operative-paragraph text (docs.un.org/S/RES/2828(2026) returned only a landing page to the fetch tool, not the document body). Checked 2026-09-24.
notes: CANONICAL, written 2026-09-24 on never-assessed initial research, superseding the shadowed proposal proposals/sudan-sanctions-regime-expiry-2026-10-09.from-unsc-haiti-gsf-mandate-expiry-2026-09-30.json (read in full before this file was written; nothing in it was contradicted). WHAT THE DATE ACTUALLY IS: not a Council session or a vote — 9 October is the day the 1591 regime's measures (arms embargo, targeted travel ban and asset freeze on designated Darfur actors) and the one-month rollover resolution 2828 created lapse absent further Council action; the Panel of Experts' own mandate runs one month longer, to 9 November. WHY THIS ROLLOVER IS MORE CONTESTED THAN THE HAITI PRECEDENT IT WAS DISCOVERED FROM: the U.S. sponsored 2828 while separately pushing to expand the arms embargo from Darfur to all of Sudan and widen designation criteria (sexual violence, kidnapping, attacks on aid workers); Russia, China, the A3 (DRC/Liberia/Somalia) and Pakistan opposed that expansion and stated a preference for a plain one-year renewal at the existing Darfur-only scope; China's own explanation of vote separately warned against forcing through contentious text. None of that bloc opposed the sanctions regime's continuation, only its scope — so the fight is over what gets renewed, not whether. This is the first time in the 1591 regime's ~21-year history (established by resolution 1591, 2005) that its annual renewal was replaced by a one-month emergency rollover rather than a full-term renewal, which this file reads as a measurable rise in friction, not a lapse signal: the regime has never lapsed. WHY low IMPACT AND symbols: [] ARE THE HONEST FILING: this book holds no Sudan- or Darfur-listed instrument (there isn't one — Sudan's own bourse is not accessible to this account and no US-listed pure play exists), and the two candidate indirect channels are both too diffuse to name a symbol against: Sudan/Darfur gold (much of it artisanal and RSF-linked financing, per UN Panel of Experts reporting) is a rounding error against global mine supply that GC=F prices, and the Port Sudan pipeline carrying South Sudan's crude exports is a transit corridor, not a source barrel, that CL=F/BZ=F do not key on. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY MOVE THIS: a resolution at or near 10-09 that lapses the regime outright (never happened in 21 years) or a veto (Russia has voted for the regime's continuation every prior year including this one's rollover). WHAT WOULD FIRM THE DATE: resolution 2828's own operative-paragraph text, still not fetched by this or the prior session — main.un.org/securitycouncil/en/content/sres27932025-style direct access to docs.un.org kept returning a landing page rather than the document body.
